## Summary

The 2026-09-26 leaked-`GIT_DIR` incident (SA-0MUIA3OE40001QJX) was rooted in a repository-override git environment variable exported into agent/test sessions by a launcher **outside** the `skill/` tree. Defence-in-depth now neutralises the *effect* at every in-repo execution path, but the launcher can still export a live-repo `GIT_DIR` (plus `GIT_WORK_TREE` / `GIT_CONFIG*`) into the **pre-scrub** environment of any process that calls `git` directly. This item investigates that export and removes or scopes it at its source.

## Problem statement

On 2026-09-26 an orphaned audit fan-out inherited `GIT_DIR=<live worktree git dir>`, `GIT_EXEC_PATH=/usr/lib/git-core` and `GIT_PREFIX=` from a launcher outside the `skill/` tree. The in-repo defence-in-depth layers (shared env scrub, release-gate fail-fast, host-wide audit cap) stop that value from reaching test subprocesses, but they remain the only protection: anything spawned before the scrub that calls `git` itself can still be redirected into the live checkout. The exporting process has not been identified and no setter exists inside this repository.

## Users

- **Agent operators / maintainers** running autonomous agents through herdr/Pi: need every freshly launched agent/test session to inherit no repository-override git variables.
- **Contributors** sharing the live checkout: need `dev`/`origin/dev` protected even when a launcher is misconfigured.

User stories:

- As an operator, I want a freshly launched agent/test session to inherit no repository-override git variables, so a misconfigured launcher can never redirect a git command into the live checkout.
- As a maintainer, I want the process that sets the override identified and fixed at source, so the defence-in-depth scrub is not the only line of protection.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The exporting process/script is identified with reproducible, non-destructive evidence (environment of a freshly spawned agent session or a traced process ancestry), and the evidence is recorded in the work item.
- [ ] The export is removed or scoped at source so child processes — panes, `audit_runner`, `run_tests`, and direct `git` calls — never inherit a live-repo `GIT_DIR` / `GIT_WORK_TREE` / `GIT_CONFIG*`.
- [ ] A regression check asserts a freshly launched agent/test session has no repository-override variables before any git-touching step; it fails if such a variable is reintroduced.
- [ ] `docs/dev/test-isolation.md` §9.3 (residual launcher risk) is updated to name the confirmed source and the fix, or to record why the source could not be confirmed.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Non-destructive investigation.** The live checkout must never be mutated; evidence gathering must use throwaway/fixture repositories and must never point `GIT_DIR` at the live repo.
- **Source, not symptom.** The fix must be at the exporting launcher, not merely another in-repo scrub layer.
- **Cross-repo.** The likely launcher lives in the ContextHub repository (`packages/herdr`), outside this worklog's repo — see Open Question 1.

## Existing state

Defence-in-depth landed under SA-0MUIA3OE40001QJX:

- `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py` — `REPOSITORY_OVERRIDE_ENV_VARS` + `scrub_repository_overrides` / `repository_override_vars_present` / `log_repository_override_scrub`.
- `skill/test_cache.py::_default_runner`, `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py::_run_cmd`, `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py::_call_pi` pass scrubbed `env=`.
- `run_tests.py --strict-git-env` release-gate fail-fast (invoked by `.githooks/pre-push` for `dev`/`main`).
- `audit_runner.main` host-wide audit cap + `_find_orphaned_audit_processes` / `_warn_on_orphaned_audits`.
- `docs/dev/test-isolation.md` §9.3 documents the residual external-launcher risk.

Confirmed by search (`rg 'export GIT_|GIT_DIR='` across the repo and tooling): **no setter exists in the SorraAgents repository**. Candidate launchers identified:

- **herdr agent launcher** (ContextHub, external): `packages/herdr/shared/send-to-pi.sh` → `packages/herdr/shared/run-pi-agent.sh`, invoked as `herdr pane run <pane> exec bash run-pi-agent.sh <lease> ...`.
- **herdr downtime worker** (external): `buildDowntimeSpawnOptions` in `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` forwards `...process.env` to `send-to-pi.sh`, adding only `HERDR_RESOLVED_CWD` and `AUDIT_PHASE2_PARALLELISM`. It does **not** scrub repository-override vars, so a `GIT_DIR` already present in the herdr process propagates to every spawned pane.
- **git-hook chain** (in repo): `.git/hooks/post-checkout|post-merge|post-rewrite` delegate to `~/.config/pi/.githooks/worklog-post-pull` → `wl sync`. Git sets `GIT_DIR`, `GIT_EXEC_PATH` and `GIT_PREFIX` when running hooks, and `implement.py`'s `git_worktree_add` (`git worktree add`) triggers `post-checkout`. The observed `GIT_EXEC_PATH=/usr/lib/git-core` + empty `GIT_PREFIX` are the exact git-hook signature, so the poisoned environment was most plausibly inherited from a git-spawned child rather than a static shell `export`.

## Desired change

1. Determine the **origin** of `GIT_DIR` in the launcher environment — which process first set it and why — using non-destructive evidence: `/proc/<pid>/environ` of pane/agent/audit processes, git `trace2` (`GIT_TRACE2_EVENT`) around `git worktree add`/hooks, and launcher/hook inspection.
2. Fix at source: scrub (or refuse to propagate) `REPOSITORY_OVERRIDE_ENV_VARS` in the launcher spawn path (e.g. herdr `buildDowntimeSpawnOptions`, `run-pi-agent.sh`/`send-to-pi.sh`) and/or stop the git-hook child that leaks the variables.
3. Add a regression check that a fresh agent/test session has no repository-override variables.
4. Update §9.3 with the finding and fix.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `docs/dev/test-isolation.md` — update §9.3 with the confirmed source and fix.
- `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py` — shared override-var list/scrub helper (reuse for any in-repo mitigation or regression check).
- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — fresh-session regression check and `--strict-git-env` integration.
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — orphan/env-evidence hooks for reproducing the audit fan-out condition safely.
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `git_worktree_add` flow that triggers the `post-checkout` hook.
- `.githooks/post-checkout`, `.githooks/post-merge`, `.githooks/post-rewrite`, `.githooks/worklog-post-pull` — hook chain (`wl sync`) executed by git with `GIT_DIR`/`GIT_EXEC_PATH`/`GIT_PREFIX` set.
- External (ContextHub, cross-repo — see Open Question 1): `packages/herdr/shared/send-to-pi.sh`, `packages/herdr/shared/run-pi-agent.sh`, `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` (`buildDowntimeSpawnOptions`).

## Related work

- **SA-0MUIA3OE40001QJX** – Test/audit runner leaks GIT_DIR into test subprocesses, corrupting the live checkout and origin/dev (parent incident; completed/in_review).
- Children of SA-0MUIA3OE40001QJX: SA-0MUIULHQC005MUM0 (shared scrub helper), SA-0MUIUMK9Y008SCE0 (scrub in execution paths), SA-0MUIULX49001BWGG (release-gate fail-fast), SA-0MUIULC2Y009XYM1 (regression tests), SA-0MUIUMBL8002HBYH (docs + full suite), SA-0MUIUMO7T00639FL (host-wide audit cap + orphan detection).
- **SA-0MUJ2VMF7000UHCX** – Restore wl sync: main-checkout git identity was left as incident-era `T <t@t.com>` (residual incident recovery).
- **SA-0MUIBWORE001HOLK** – Symlink nested node_modules into implement worktrees (the worktree whose git dir appeared in the leaked `GIT_DIR`).

### Related work (automated report)

- **SA-0MS0DK6BD001RNDG** – implement.py abort script deletes entire project directory when aborting from main working tree (completed)
- **SA-0MSAXHMZT009EHVV** – cwd-independent wl invocation and real diagnostics (completed)
- **SA-0MPDZDVG00013CQJ** – Implement: Agent push-to-dev behavior (completed)

Repository file matches: `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`, `docs/dev/test-isolation.md`, `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md`.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk:** the incident evidence (process env at the time) is gone; reproduction could itself endanger the live checkout. **Mitigation:** use a throwaway repo + `GIT_TRACE2_EVENT`; never point `GIT_DIR` at the live repo.
- **Risk:** fixing only the identified launcher leaves other propagation paths. **Mitigation:** scrub at the launcher spawn boundary (one choke point) plus the regression check.
- **Risk (scope creep):** hardening every launcher is broader than this investigation. **Mitigation:** record additional opportunities as linked work items rather than expanding this item.
- **Assumption:** the leak is architectural (environment propagation through the launcher) rather than a one-off manual `export`.
- **Assumption:** the `GIT_EXEC_PATH`/`GIT_PREFIX` signature indicates a git-spawned child origin; if tracing shows otherwise, the evidence will redirect the fix.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 (scope / repo):** The candidate launchers are external to SorraAgents (ContextHub `packages/herdr`) and the git-hook chain that runs `wl sync`. Where should the fix land? Options: (A) investigate + evidence in SorraAgents (this item); if herdr is the culprit, file a cross-repo ContextHub work item and link it; (B) fix entirely within SorraAgents by hardening the git hooks / adding a wrapper; (C) transfer this item to ContextHub. **Recommended:** A — keeps the incident record in SorraAgents while routing the actual code change to the repo that owns the launcher. — **OPEN QUESTION** (producer input required).
- **Q2 (reproduction):** How much live reproduction is acceptable? ## Summary
On a shared host with several agents running implement/test/audit concurrently, the full suite produced environment-induced failures with no code defect:

1. `tests/test_live_repo_mutation_guard.py::TestRunTestsGuardFires::*` and
   `tests/test_pytest_path_resolution.py::test_run_tests_spawns_resolved_pytest_when_missing`

   `run_tests.py --scope full` invocation waits for the host-wide "test" semaphore
   (max 2) and exceeds the spawning test's 180 s subprocess timeout.
2. The `live_repo_guard` plugin reports "live-repo mutation detected" at teardown
   when **other agents** push to `origin` (observed `refs/remotes/origin/dev` and
   `refs/heads/wl-*` moving mid-run), even though the suite itself did not mutate
   the checkout.

## Evidence
- SA-0MSN2LIOQ004TON1 validation: an armed full run gave 3249 passed / 0 failures
  with 3 guard teardown errors; another armed run gave 3246 passed / 3 failures

  guard stood down passed 3247 with only the guard's own 2 tests failing (expected).
  The failing set changes run-to-run, confirming non-determinism.

- Make the nested-runner tests resilient to test-semaphore saturation (raise/derive
  their subprocess timeout, or inject a test-only slot/`TEST_LOCK_TIMEOUT`).

  live-repo guard fingerprint, or only arming it for refs the suite can create.

- AC1: Nested `run_tests.py` tests do not time out purely because the host test
  semaphore is busy.
- AC2: The live-repo guard does not fail a run when only external `origin/*` refs move.

## Problem

The audit runner's terminal lifecycle can compute an **invalid** pre-audit status+stage pair and then fail to apply it, leaving the audited work item's lifecycle unresolved.

Observed on `SA-0MSITKWBP007VUJS` during `/skill:audit` (2026-09-27, commit `e365fce2`):

- Captured pre-audit state: `status=blocked`, `stage=in_review`.
- The run ended with an infrastructure-fallback `No` (parent Phase 1 Pi calls stalled — `Local Proxy/plan`, no output for 600 s each), so the restore branch ran with `safe_status=blocked`, `safe_stage=in_review`.
- `wl update --status blocked --stage in_review` was rejected:
  `Invalid status/stage combination: status "blocked" is not compatible with stage "in_review". Allowed stages for status "blocked": idea, intake_complete, plan_complete.`
- After 3 retries, `_restore_pre_audit_state_on_failure` attempted the same invalid pair and also failed:
  `The item's lifecycle is unresolved — check its state with wl show ... and recover manually if needed.`
- `wl doctor` flags the same item as `status-stage.incompatible` with safe fix `status=completed`.

## Root cause

In `_apply_terminal_lifecycle` the restore branch uses `safe_stage = ctx.original_stage` verbatim; the fallback stage is only computed when the stage is empty (`if not safe_stage`). The captured pair is never validated against worklog's `statusStageCompatibility`, so an already-incompatible stored pair is propagated unchanged and rejected by `wl update`.

## Proposed change

Normalise the target pair to a compatible status+stage **before** issuing the `wl update`:

- If `original_stage` is not valid for `original_status`, choose a valid stage (e.g. `plan_complete` for `blocked`, matching the existing empty-stage fallback) or the `wl doctor` safe fix (`status=completed` for stage `in_review`).
- Verify the pair is accepted; surface the normalisation in the diagnostic.
- Apply the same normalisation in `_restore_pre_audit_state_on_failure`.

## Acceptance criteria

1. When the captured pre-audit state is an incompatible status+stage pair (e.g. `blocked`+`in_review`), the terminal restore applies a **valid** pair and verifies it via readback — the item is never left with an unresolved lifecycle.
2. A regression test captures an item whose pre-audit state is an incompatible pair and asserts the terminal lifecycle ends in a valid state (and never retries the known-invalid pair).
3. The runner's diagnostic states the incompatible pair and the normalised pair it applied.
4. Full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Observed

During SA-0MUOO5UEB008RXBP, `implement.py finish` reported `git push to dev failed` and reset the work item to `open` (removing the worktree), but the commit had actually landed on `origin/dev` (origin/dev == dev == 4b25aac4, new file present). `cleanup.terminated: 1` was reported.

## Impact

False failure resets a successfully-implemented item to `open`, risking duplicate work and leaving the item un-in\_review despite the work being on dev. The operator/agent must manually detect and correct the state.

## Likely cause (to confirm)

The push step resolves its timeout from `.pi/test-config.json` `timeoutPerCommand` (1500s) and kills the process group on timeout; the pre-push hook runs the full suite. If the hook/ push exceeds the bound after the remote has accepted the objects, the command is killed and reported as a failure even though the push completed.

## AC

1. `implement.py finish` distinguishes 'push completed' from 'push command interrupted after completion' (e.g. verify the remote ref advanced / commit reachable on origin before reporting failure).
2. On a push that actually landed, the item is advanced to `completed/in_review` (not reset to open) and the commit comment recorded.
3. Regression test covering the push-completed-but-hook-interrupted path.
4. Full suite passes.

# implement.py parent misclassifies soft-deleted children

## Problem
`implement.py parent <parent-id>` treats a child whose `deletedBy` is set (soft-deleted; `status` remains `open`) as implementable. `_classify_child` in `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` only checks `status` against `TERMINAL_STATUSES` ({in_review, completed, done, deleted}); it never inspects `deletedBy`. As a result `phase_parent` calls `phase_start` on the soft-deleted child, creates a bogus worktree/branch, claims the item `in_progress`, and stops the chain instead of advancing the parent.

## Reproduction
`wl delete <child>` on a child of an epic sets `deletedBy` but leaves `status: open` (verified with SA-0MUD5SYC0002SX5X / SA-0MUD5U06J009V0EK, both `deletedBy: plan`). Running `implement.py parent SA-0MUA4Q431008HIH0` then started a worktree for SA-0MUD5SYC0002SX5X and set it `in-progress`, even though both real children were `completed`.

## Expected
A child with `deletedBy` set must be treated as terminal (`skip-terminal`): never claimed, never given a worktree, and never allowed to block parent advancement.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `_classify_child` treats `deletedBy` (non-empty) as terminal regardless of `status`.
- [ ] `phase_parent` advances a parent whose only non-terminal statuses are soft-deleted children.
- [ ] Soft-deleted children count as terminal when gating in-chain blockers, so a child blocked only by a soft-deleted sibling is still startable (terminal determination must be consistent with `_classify_child`, not status-only).
- [ ] Regression test: a soft-deleted child is skipped and the parent advances.

# PriorityQueue directory lock ignores timeouts — audit slot acquisition can block indefinitely

## Goal (user story)

As an agent running an audit, I want every queue operation in the slot-admission
path to honour its configured timeout, so a peer that holds the queue directory
lock cannot make slot acquisition hang forever.

## Problem statement

`skill/shared/queue.py:282` (`PriorityQueue._acquire_lock`) takes a **blocking**
`fcntl.flock(fd, fcntl.LOCK_EX)` with **no timeout**:

```python
def _acquire_lock(self) -> None:
    lock_path = self._queue_dir / ".lock"
    lock_path.touch(exist_ok=True)
    fd = os.open(str(lock_path), os.O_RDWR)
    fcntl.flock(fd, fcntl.LOCK_EX)      # blocks indefinitely
    self._lock_fd = fd
```

Every public queue operation (`enqueue`, `dequeue`, `peek`, `remove`, `rank`,
`__len__`, `_list_entries`) acquires this lock via `with self._locked()`.
`_acquire_audit_slot()` (audit_runner.py) calls `queue.enqueue`, `queue.rank`,
`queue.peek` and `queue.remove`, so a peer holding `.lock` blocks audit slot
acquisition **without any bound**, defeating the `AUDIT_QUEUE_TIMEOUT`
(default 90 s) and `AUDIT_LOCK_TIMEOUT` (default 0 s, fail-fast) guarantees.

## Evidence

Minimal reproduction — a child process holds the queue lock for 6 s; the parent
calls `peek(timeout=0)`, whose contract is fail-fast:

```
$ python3 /tmp/queue_hang_demo.py
peek(timeout=0) blocked for 5.50s (contract: ~0s)
```

The timeout argument is not consulted because `_acquire_lock()` blocks **before**
any deadline check. Confirmed against `skill/shared/queue.py` at `dev`
(commit 88a404ec).

## Impact

- A process parked inside the critical section (SIGSTOP, deep I/O stall on the
  lock directory, or a long `_prune_stale` sweep) makes every concurrent audit's
  slot acquisition hang indefinitely — the exact "audit slot acquisition hangs
  indefinitely" symptom reported by an agent (mis-attributed to an unreachable
  `localhost:8000` proxy).
- The priority-queue admission contract (bounded wait, then raise
  `TimeoutError` → "concurrency limit reached" verdict) is not honoured against
  lock contention.
- Contrast: the same package's `Semaphore` uses `LOCK_EX | LOCK_NB` with a
  bounded retry loop, so this is an inconsistency within the shared layer.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `PriorityQueue` lock acquisition is **bounded**: a peer holding the directory
   lock cannot block `_acquire_lock`/any public op beyond the configured
   timeout.
2. The configured timeout is honoured on the lock-acquisition path:
   `enqueue` raises `TimeoutError` on deadline, and `dequeue`/`peek` return
   `None` on empty/deadline **without** blocking past it.
3. Implementation follows the existing `Semaphore` pattern (non-blocking
   `LOCK_EX | LOCK_NB` + short retry loop with a monotonic deadline) or an
   equivalent bounded mechanism; no busy-spin without sleep.
4. Re-entrant behaviour within a single `PriorityQueue` instance is preserved
   (nested `_locked()` remains a no-op when already held).
5. A regression test holds the lock from a second process and asserts that a
   `peek(timeout=0)`/`enqueue(timeout=small)` returns/raises within a bounded
   margin rather than blocking for the hold duration.
6. Existing queue tests (skill/shared/tests/) and the full suite pass.

## Key Files

- `skill/shared/queue.py` — `_acquire_lock`, `_release_lock`, `_locked`,
  `enqueue`, `dequeue`, `peek`, `remove`, `rank`.
- `skill/shared/tests/` — queue tests.
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — `_acquire_audit_slot` (consumer).

## Constraints

- Cross-process mutual exclusion must be preserved (no lost updates).
- No new required configuration; existing env vars (`AUDIT_QUEUE_TIMEOUT`,
  `AUDIT_LOCK_TIMEOUT`, `QUEUE_MAX_DEPTH`, `QUEUE_TTL_SECONDS`) keep working.
- flock releases on process exit / crash must remain the stale-lock guarantee.

## Related Work

- discovered-from:SA-0MUV2UBMT008OE2E (audit slot-status endpoint hardcodes
  localhost). The localhost default was a real bug but **not** the cause of the
  reported hang; this item is the actual unbounded-blocking path.
- SA-0MTG5RYH8005RQNM — priority-queue admission (`AUDIT_QUEUE_TIMEOUT`).
- SA-0MSCC02ME009EGCB — prior audit concurrency investigation.

## Problem

The global implement skill's parent phase (`implement.py parent`) has two gaps that cause epics to loop when a child is externally blocked:

1. **`do-not-delegate` is not honoured.** The herdr dispatcher respects the `do-not-delegate` tag, but `implement.py parent` does not: `_classify_child` returns "implement" for any non-terminal, non-in-progress child and `_next_child_to_implement` selects it regardless of the tag. An epic whose only startable child is guard-tagged will therefore be repeatedly selected and its guarded child re-attempted on every dispatch.

2. **Stale worktree branches are not reused or cleaned.** `git_worktree_add` runs `git worktree add --track -b <branch> <path> <parent>`, which fails if `<branch>` already exists. When a prior `start` aborted after creating the branch but before/at worktree removal, the branch survives and every subsequent `start` fails with a cryptic "Failed to create worktree" error instead of reusing the branch or reporting the stale branch clearly.

Observed on **Switch game audio from procedural Web Audio to ToneForge (AH-0MUTUOB7X007PR9J)** (session herdr-1791234333-893049-2032): `implement.py parent` selected the externally-blocked, `do-not-delegate` child **Author game-specific ToneForge recipes (AH-0MUTYV8480019Z51)** and then failed worktree creation because the branch `wl-AH-0MUTYV8480019Z51-author-game-specific-toneforge-recipes` already existed.

## Expected behaviour

- `implement.py parent` skips `do-not-delegate` children (reports them as guarded/not startable) unless explicitly overridden.
- `git_worktree_add` either reuses an existing branch that is identical to / fast-forwardable from the parent branch, or fails with an actionable message naming the stale branch and how to recover.
- A failed `start` should not leave a stale branch behind (or should clean it up on abort).

## Scope

- Global implement skill script `~/.pi/agent/skills/implement/scripts/implement.py` (`_classify_child`, `_next_child_to_implement`, `git_worktree_add`, `phase_start`/abort path). This is agent-infrastructure code; report/plan changes there, do not edit from an AI_Hell worktree.

# Ship release must verify in-scope work items are actually closed before reporting success

## Problem

`closeWorkItemsAfterRelease()` in `skill/ship/scripts/run-release.js` closes each
candidate with `wl close <id> --force --reason "Shipped in v<version>"` and treats a zero
exit code as success. It never re-reads the item to confirm the persisted
`status`/`stage`. The release then prints `All N work item(s) closed successfully.` — even
when some closes did not persist.

This was demonstrated by the ToneForge v0.1.2 release (2026-10-06): the close step
reported **53/53** closed, but only **50** items ended up `completed`/`done`. Three
remained `completed`/`in_review` with no close comment and unchanged `updatedAt`:

| Item | Title |
|---|---|
| TF-0MUUC9RTU008UJ18 | Add CLI command to register new primitive recipes |
| TF-0MUUELBUD002OEQ8 | Repair main checkout node_modules symlink loop blocking npm/vitest |
| TF-0MMZIW9NQ09MV98G | Convert hard-coded recipes to ToneGraph configs |

Root cause is the `wl` lost-update race fixed/tracked in ContextHub: a concurrent
`wl sync` clobbered the three in-flight closes (see **WL-0MUXA5RI2009EUTJ** under
WL-0MUVSQ4EO00092E7). The ship skill cannot prevent that race, but it **can** detect it:
right now a lost close is silently reported as a successful release.

## Desired behaviour

After the close step, re-read every attempted candidate and confirm it is terminal
(`status == "completed"` and `stage == "done"`). If any are not:

1. Re-attempt the close once (bounded), then re-verify.
2. Report unclosed items explicitly by id in the release summary — never include them in
   the "closed" count or claim "all closed successfully".
3. Make the discrepancy visible in the step result (e.g. `unclosedCount` /
   `unclosedItems`) so the operator sees the true outcome.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `closeWorkItemsAfterRelease()` verifies persisted state (injectable read boundary) for
   each attempted close instead of trusting only the close command's exit code.
2. An item that exits 0 but is not `completed`/`done` is counted as unclosed and listed by
   id; the summary/return value reflects it and does not claim blanket success.
3. A transient lost close is retried at least once before being reported unclosed.
4. Regression tests with injected `getCandidateItemsFn` / `runCloseCommand` /
   verification boundary cover: (a) all closes persist → success; (b) one close is a no-op
   (exit 0, state unchanged) → retried, then reported unclosed; (c) retry re-persists →
   reported closed.
5. `npm run build` and existing ship suites pass.

## Notes

- Root-cause fix is on the `wl` side: WL-0MUXA5RI2009EUTJ (lock `wl close`; child of the
  WL-0MUVSQ4EO00092E7 lost-update umbrella).
- Related: SA-0MUJKPDAA002VVDP (close step *falsely refuses* parents with done
  descendants — fixed by SA-0MUTYRYUG008A4A9 / SA-0MUTYRYEM000EEF7).
- Refiled to ContextHub: SA-0MUX8PYAY0008HFZ (the raw race report) → WL-0MUXA5RI2009EUTJ.

Discovered while implementing SA-0MUMHR0BT007IKAL (discovered-from:SA-0MUMHR0BT007IKAL).

## Problem
Two or more full test-suite runs executing concurrently on the same host deadlock. Observed twice today: two pytest full-suite processes (one per agent worktree) both stalled in hrtimer_nanosleep with <30s CPU after ~30-40 min, and both recovered only when one run was killed (the surviving run resumed immediately).

## Root cause (hypothesis)
TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY defaults to 2. Each outer run_tests.py holds one `test` semaphore slot for the duration of the suite. The suite itself contains tests that invoke nested `run_tests.py` (tests/test_live_repo_mutation_guard.py::TestRunTestsGuardFires) which need another `test` slot. With two outer runs holding both slots, the nested acquires wait indefinitely (TEST_LOCK_TIMEOUT inherited from the parent, e.g. 10800s), producing a deadlock. Setting TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY=4 for one run let its nested acquires use the spare slots and avoided the deadlock.

## Secondary flake
tests/unit/test-post-release-dev-sync.mjs calls syncDevWithMain() which runs live `git fetch`/`git push` against the real repo; under concurrent load it hung in ep_poll (socket) and blocked the pre-push full-suite gate. This test is non-hermetic and should be made hermetic (inject/fake the git operations).

## Desired outcome
- Full-suite runs on a shared host must not deadlock (reserve headroom for nested run_tests slots, or make the nested-aware tests use an isolated semaphore dir / PI_SEMAPHORE_DIR).
- tests/unit/test-post-release-dev-sync.mjs must not perform live git fetch/push.

## Evidence
- /tmp/finish-SA-0MUMHR0BT007IKAL.log (slot wait + full-suite gate).
- Kill of one stalled pytest unstuck the other (wchan hrtimer_nanosleep -> poll_schedule_timeout -> R).

## Problem

The local skill extensions convention (`.pi/skills_extensions/<skill>/`, contract SA-0MSQ7MQEJ0064ZB0) is consumed only by the test skill. The implement skill never calls `load_extension()`, so a project-local extension for implement is inert: its `SKILL_PREFIX.md` is never surfaced and its `extension.json` is ignored.

This blocks consuming projects that need project-specific implement behaviour — concretely, `open_source_llm` (OSL-0MUYC0UEN003C1M6) wants uncommitted `.llm-wiki/` content to be exempt from the dirty-tree gate.

## Expected

- `implement.py` loads `.pi/skills_extensions/implement/` via the shared `load_extension()` helper; absence is a no-op (byte-for-byte unchanged behaviour).
- Project-local prose hooks (`SKILL_PREFIX.md` / `SKILL_POSTFIX.md`) are surfaced to the agent at the documented points.
- A project can declare that specific dirty paths are expected and must not hard-fail `implement.py start`/`finish`; the exemption is project-scoped, explicit, and additive (never weakens the build → test → commit order).
- The worktree placement gate (`_worktree_placement_violation()`) uses the same exemption logic.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Absent extension: implement behaviour is unchanged.

# Intake Brief: Tighten plan-approval-gate to largest and highest risk only

## Problem statement

The plan skill's approval gate currently requests producer approval when effort is **Medium/Large/Extra Large** **OR** risk is **High/Severe**. The user considers this too broad and wants approval gated only for the **largest and highest risk** work items — Extra Large effort **AND** High/Severe risk.

## Users

- **AI agents** running `/skill:plan` — benefit from fewer unnecessary interruptions on medium-effort or medium-risk items that are safe to proceed on.
- **Human operators / producers** — receive approval requests only for genuinely large-scale, high-risk plans that warrant their attention.

Example user stories:

- "As a developer running `/skill:plan` on a Small-effort, Low-risk item, I want the plan to proceed directly to the automated review stages without asking me to approve, so the workflow is not interrupted unnecessarily."
- "As a developer running `/skill:plan` on a Large-effort, Medium-risk item, I want the plan to proceed without my approval, so small-to-medium items are not blocked on me unnecessarily."
- "As a developer running `/skill:plan` on an Extra Large-effort, High-risk item, I want to be asked to approve the plan AND be told why, so I understand why a human checkpoint is required."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. When the plan skill produces a feature plan for a work item with effort **Extra Large** **AND** risk **High or Severe**, it asks the user to accept/edit/reorder the plan, and the approval question explicitly states the reason.
2. For all other effort/risk combinations (including Medium/Large effort with High risk, Extra Large effort with Medium risk, Small effort with any risk, etc.), the plan proceeds directly to the automated review stages without an approval pause.
3. When effort and/or risk values are absent from the work item, the approval gate defaults conservatively to requesting approval (a human checkpoint is never silently skipped).
4. The gating logic is covered by automated tests covering the full effort × risk matrix, including the new AND threshold.
5. The `SKILL.md` documentation is updated to reflect the new AND gate logic.
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Reuse the existing effort/risk decision logic in `plan_helpers.py` (`resolve_complexity_tier`, effort t-shirt sizes, risk levels) — do not introduce a parallel complexity model.
- The approval gate reads the same effort/risk values computed by the effort-and-risk skill during the pre-check.
- "Largest" = Extra Large effort (the top of the t-shirt scale). "Highest risk" = High or Severe risk.
- The change is strictly confined to the `should_request_plan_approval` gate and the `plan-approval-gate` CLI; the pre-check skip/plan logic is unaffected.

## Existing state

- `skill/plan/plan_helpers.py`: `should_request_plan_approval()` (line ~351) uses **OR** logic — `effort in PLAN_APPROVAL_EFFORT` (Medium/Large/Extra Large) **or** `risk in PLAN_APPROVAL_RISK` (High/Severe).
- `skill/plan/SKILL.md`: Plan-approval gate section instructs presenting the plan for approval when the gate returns True.
- `PLAN_APPROVAL_EFFORT = frozenset({"Medium", "Large", "Extra Large"})` — line 66.
- `PLAN_APPROVAL_RISK = frozenset({"High", "Severe"})` — line 67.
- **SA-0MSHID94D009P0TL** (completed): "Conditional plan approval gating" — introduced the current OR-based gate.
- **SA-0MUIUTJJS008W06Y** (open): "plan-approval-gate skips checkpoint for t-shirt effort and Severe risk" — vocabulary normalisation bug (separate from this change).

## Desired change

- Change `should_request_plan_approval` from **OR** to **AND** logic: approval is requested only when effort is Extra Large **AND** risk is High or Severe.
- Narrow `PLAN_APPROVAL_EFFORT` to `frozenset({"Extra Large"})` (or adjust the comparison to check for Extra Large specifically).
- Update the `plan-approval-gate` CLI to reflect the new AND gate.
- Update the reason string logic so the reason describes both conditions being met (e.g., "its effort is Extra Large scale and its risk is High").
- Update `SKILL.md` documentation to reflect the new AND gate logic.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/plan/plan_helpers.py` — Change `should_request_plan_approval()` from OR to AND logic; narrow `PLAN_APPROVAL_EFFORT` or adjust the comparison.
- `skill/plan/SKILL.md` — Update the Plan-approval gate section to describe the new AND gate.
- `skill/plan/tests/test_plan_helpers.py` — Update unit tests: the old OR-combination test cases should now expect `request_approval: false`, and add explicit AND-combination tests.

## Related work

- **SA-0MSHID94D009P0TL** — "Conditional plan approval gating in plan skill" (completed). Introduced the current OR-based gate.
- **SA-0MUIUTJJS008W06Y** — "plan-approval-gate skips checkpoint for t-shirt effort and Severe risk" (open). Vocabulary normalisation bug — may need attention first but is a separate issue.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk:** agents may submit plans that are larger or riskier than expected without a human checkpoint. Mitigation: the six automated review stages still run before `plan_complete`, and the tree_coverage review verifies AC coverage.
- **Risk:** this is a behavioural change that could surprise operators accustomed to more frequent approval requests. Mitigation: the SKILL.md documentation is updated, and the reason string explicitly states what triggered the gate.
- **Assumption:** "largest" = Extra Large (top of the t-shirt scale). "Highest risk" = High or Severe (top two risk levels). This is stated by the user directly.
- **Assumption:** the change applies only to the plan-approval gate in step 4, not to other gates in the plan skill (e.g., step 5 phasing check, which is exception-driven).
- **Scope-creep risk:** any additional approval-gate ideas (e.g., making thresholds configurable, gating other steps) should be recorded as linked work items rather than expanding this item's scope.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: What does "largest and highest risk" mean precisely? — Answer (operator, direct directive): largest = Extra Large effort (top of the t-shirt scale), highest risk = High or Severe risk level. **Recommended:** use Extra Large AND High/Severe — matches the operator's intent for the strictest possible gate.
- Q: Should absent effort/risk still default to requesting approval? — Answer: yes, conservatively — a human checkpoint is never silently skipped.
- Q: Does this change apply to the auto-complete/skip path? — Answer: no-op by construction — the skip path produces no feature plan, so no approval question applies.

# implement.py start fails to claim an open work item (invalid stage)

## Problem
With the installed Worklog CLI (wl 0.1.19), `wl update --stage in_progress` is rejected: valid stages are `idea, intake_complete, plan_complete, in_review, done`. `phase_start` in `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` claims via `StatusLifecycle.update_status(id, 'in_progress', stage='in_progress', ...)`, so claiming an `open` item fails outright:

```
wl ... update SA-... --status in_progress --json --stage in_progress --assignee Map
RuntimeError: Invalid stage "in_progress". Valid stages: idea, intake_complete, plan_complete, in_review, done.
```

When the item is already `in-progress`, only the stage update fails and `phase_start` logs a WARNING and proceeds. When the item is `open`, the combined update fails and `implement.py start` returns `success: false` — the normal (open -> in_progress) claim path is broken.

## Impact
Every `implement.py start` / `finish` on a freshly-opened item cannot claim it; agents must claim manually with a status-only update. Blocks the deterministic implement workflow.

## Expected
Claiming sets `status=in_progress` without an invalid stage (preserve the current stage or use a valid one). The StatusLifecycle claim path should not pass `stage='in_progress'` on a wl build that does not accept it.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `implement.py start <id>` on an `open` item succeeds and sets `status=in_progress`.
- [ ] No `--stage in_progress` is sent to `wl` (or it is only sent when the installed wl supports it).
- [ ] Regression test asserts the claim path does not fail on a wl build whose stage enum excludes `in_progress`.
